case_title: Raja Gounder & Anr. v. State of Tamil Nadu
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC; sentence not stated in judgment
high_court_outcome: Conviction affirmed (Crl. A. No. 573 of 2001, judgment dated 09.07.2004, found against the appellants)
neutral_facts: The victim was killed in a fatal assault during the night. The accused were the victim's brothers, and relations between the parties had been strained by a dispute over land. The incident occurred at about 10.00 p.m. at a short distance from the victim's house. The victim's wife had seen the attack on her husband. She first sent word to her parents in their village and then went to the police station, and the first information report was lodged about 13 hours after the incident. The victim's sister and the accused's mother were cited as prosecution witnesses. No independent witness was examined, and the case rested on the account of the victim's wife. The first information report referred to two injuries on the victim, whereas the post-mortem examination detected eight injuries. The medical evidence was examined against the eyewitness account, and the attack took place in the dark of night.
physical_harm: Death of the victim; eight injuries detected at post-mortem
motive: Land dispute between the brothers (accepted by courts below as the motive)
key_evidence_accepted: Ocular testimony of PW.1 (victim's wife); post-mortem and medical evidence found consistent with it
witness_credibility: PW.1 found credible; delay and absence of independent witness explained; later resiling by parents viewed as common in fratricides
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 09.07.2004; Supreme Court: 28.09.2010
legal_representation: Appellants: K. Sarada Devi; Respondent (State): S. Thananjayan
investigation_status: FIR lodged about 13 hours after incident; charge sheet and later stages not stated
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302; High Court (Crl. A. No. 573 of 2001, 09.07.2004): conviction upheld; Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
defence_argument: Delay of 13 hours in FIR unexplained and used to fabricate story; sister and mother cited but not produced; FIR named two injuries though eight found at post-mortem
legal_principle_applied: Delay in FIR explained by conduct of a young widow; absence of independent witness acceptable in family dispute; minor variance with ocular and medical evidence not fatal; interference declined
